What they need from AI and digital work differs, and so do our engagements.

sections.h: Texas privacy and AI law, built in
p: The Texas Data Privacy and Security Act has applied since July 2024. It gives Texas residents rights over their personal data, requires clear privacy notices, and requires data protection assessments for higher-risk processing such as targeted advertising, sale of data and sensitive data. The Texas Attorney General enforces it.

Texas also passed the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act, which takes effect in 2026 and sets rules on certain uses of AI, including disclosure duties for government bodies and healthcare providers. We map which systems touch personal data, keep sensitive data out of tools that should not see it and document the decisions, so your counsel can review quickly. We are not a law firm and your legal team keeps the final word.

On-site visits happen when the project needs it, for example a workshop with an operations team or a launch day. Day to day, work runs through video calls, a shared project board and weekly written updates from your Signal Lead.

list: Talk: a 15-minute fit check, then a longer discovery session with the people who own the problem
Plan: a written plan with use cases ranked by value and effort, costs, risks and dates
Build: a pilot on real data, measured against the baseline, then a full rollout

faqs.q: What does a first AI project with a Texas company usually cover?
faqs.a: Usually one process with a clear cost, such as document intake, quoting or reporting. We map how it works today, agree what success looks like, build a pilot with a person approving the output, and report results in writing before anything is rolled out further.

faqs.q: How do you handle the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act?
faqs.a: We map what personal data each system uses, keep sensitive data out of tools that do not need it, and document decisions for any processing that needs a data protection assessment. We also make sure privacy notices and consent match how the data is used. Your counsel reviews and approves the final setup.

faqs.q: Which Texas cities do you work with?
faqs.a: Dallas, Houston and Austin each have their own page on this site, and we work just as well with companies elsewhere in the state, such as San Antonio or Fort Worth. Location within Texas does not change how the engagement runs.

faqs.q: What does AI consulting cost for a Texas company?
faqs.a: It depends on scope. The main factors are how many use cases we review or build, which systems and data sources are involved, security and compliance needs, and whether you want ongoing support. After a 15-minute call we send a written scope with dates so you can compare options.

faqs.q: Can you help with marketing as well as AI?
faqs.a: Yes. We run SEO, generative engine optimization, paid media, websites, video and 3D for Texas companies, with the same lead who runs the AI and data work. That matters when an AI tool changes how you sell or serve customers, because the marketing can change with it.

faqs.q: Do you work with Texas energy and healthcare companies?
faqs.a: Yes. For energy and industrial firms the work often starts with data: cleaning operational data, building dashboards and automating reporting. For healthcare providers we plan around HIPAA and Texas law, keep patient data in tools that can sign a business associate agreement, and focus on intake, scheduling and administrative work.
